**Question.** What does an accelerant actually get to target?

```bash
uname -r; getconf PAGESIZE; grep -E 'MemTotal|Hugepagesize' /proc/meminfo; nproc
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,compute_cap,driver_version --format=csv,noheader
for i in enp1s0f1np1 enP2p1s0f1np1; do ethtool $i | awk '/Speed/{print $2}'; done
ping -c3 -W1 192.168.100.11 | tail -1
```

| property | head | peer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU | GB10, cc 12.1 (`sm_121`), driver 580.173.02 | same |
| kernel | 6.17.0-1031-nvidia-64k | same |
| page size | 65536 B | 65536 B |
| hugepage size | 512 MiB | 512 MiB |
| MemTotal | 129,735,232 kB (123.73 GiB) | 129,735,360 kB |
| CPU cores | 20 | 20 |

Memory is unified across CPU and GPU. `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total`
returns `[N/A]` on this platform, so allocator telemetry is the only authority
on GPU-visible capacity.

| fabric | value |
| --- | --- |
| links | 2, both up at 200000 Mb/s (`192.168.100.0/24`, `192.168.101.0/24`) |
| RDMA devices | 4 RoCE (`rocep1s0f0/f1`, `roceP2p1s0f0/f1`) |
| peer RTT | 0.55 ms |
| root storage | 916 GB, 544 GB free |

Cluster totals: 247.5 GiB unified memory, ~50 GB/s theoretical dual-rail
fabric.

**Verdict.** Accepted as the target baseline. Memory bandwidth is still a
datasheet number (~273 GB/s) and has not been measured.

**Reopen if.**

- either node is re-imaged, or the kernel or driver changes
